headline_marked: Cricket legend [[Sir Garry Sobers dies at 89]], hailed as greatest all-rounder
headline: Cricket legend Sir Garry Sobers dies at 89, hailed as greatest all-rounder
summary: The West Indies icon, who once hit six sixes in a single over, is remembered as one of the most complete cricketers to ever play the game.
details: Sir Garry Sobers, widely regarded as one of the greatest all-round cricketers in history, has died at the age of 89. West Indies Cricket announced the news on Friday, though no cause of death was provided.

Born in Barbados in 1936, Sobers was a destructive left-handed batsman, a skilled pace and spin bowler, and a brilliant fielder. Wisden Almanack named him one of the five leading cricketers of the 20th century.

His career was marked by extraordinary feats, including scoring 365 not out against Pakistan at age 21, which was then the highest individual test innings. He also became the first player to hit six sixes in one over in first-class cricket in 1968.
Even the legendary Don Bradman praised him, stating without hesitation that Sobers was the greatest all-round cricketer he had ever seen.

Sobers' journey began in humble circumstances, playing 'Lilliputian cricket' on beaches with balls made of tar and bats made from fence pieces. He often attributed his success to hard work rather than natural genius.
Beyond the pitch, Sobers faced controversy in 1970 for playing in apartheid Rhodesia, an act for which he later expressed deep regret, stating he had not realized the depth of feeling on the issue.
caption:
From playing with tar balls on a beach to becoming the world's greatest all-rounder. Rest in peace, Sir Garry Sobers.

headline_marked: 15 injured as [[strong tornado hits Cox's Bazar beach]]
headline: 15 injured as strong tornado hits Cox's Bazar beach
summary: A sudden and powerful tornado struck the popular tourist destination, causing panic among visitors and leaving several people injured.
details: A powerful tornado suddenly hit the Cox's Bazar beach, sparking widespread panic among the tourists and locals present at the scene.
At least 15 people were reported injured during the sudden weather event, as people scrambled for safety while the tornado touched down.
Witnesses described a scene of chaos as the strong winds and swirling debris flew through the air, causing people to run in terror.
The tornado's sudden appearance gave visitors little time to react, leading to injuries as they rushed to find cover from the wind and rain.
Local authorities and emergency responders have been managing the situation on the beach, providing assistance to the injured.
